conditional_setup: Let Q be a finite independent real box with endpoints l_j<=u_j. Substitute every fixed coordinate with l_j=u_j and work in the remaining free coordinates. Select a symbolic coordinate k with l_k<u_k and its upper facet x_k<=u_k. These are hypotheses, not properties newly checked on any saved system.

Let R be a finite collection of inequalities a_i*x<=b_i, each valid for EVERY point of Q. Retained ordinary box bounds are included in R when present. Equalities valid throughout Q can also be retained; after fixed-coordinate substitution their free-coordinate coefficients must all vanish.

Suppose R contains no row which, after fixed-coordinate substitution, is a positive multiple of x_k<=u_k. Then R does not imply x_k<=u_k over the reals. This is true even if every other facet of Q is retained.
symbolic_proof: Choose the symbolic relative-interior facet point v with v_k=u_k and l_j<v_j<u_j for every other free coordinate j. No value from saved data is chosen or substituted into this symbolic point.

Write s_i=b_i-a_i*v. Validity on Q gives s_i>=0. If s_i=0, perturbing v in both directions along any free coordinate j other than k while staying in the facet shows a_ij=0. Perturbing inward in coordinate k shows a_ik>=0.

Consequently a tight row with a_ik>0 is exactly a positive multiple of the selected upper facet. Under the hypothesis that no such row remains, every row with a_ik>0 has s_i>0. Rows with a_ik<=0 cannot be violated by increasing x_k.

Because R is finite, choose a symbolic epsilon>0 smaller than every ratio s_i/a_ik for rows with a_ik>0; if that set is empty, choose any positive epsilon. Then v+epsilon*e_k satisfies every retained inequality and every box-valid equality, but violates x_k<=u_k. All other coordinates and their retained bounds stay fixed.
The lower-facet statement follows by reversing coordinate k. Deleting additional facets cannot restore the missing implication, since the same symbolic witness already satisfies every other facet.
